result.description:
Location: Balaklava, SA, 5461
Full-Time: Immediate start
Reports to: Aged Care Facility Manager
Job Title: Personal Care Assistant
Salary range: $79,500 - $85,000 - depending on skills level and work experience + superannuation.
Job Closure date: 30 days

About the Role
On behalf of our client, an independent, not-for-profit aged care provider known as “the heart of country care,” we are seeking a compassionate Personal Care Assistant. Our client proudly supports older South Australians in regional communities with safe, caring, and inclusive living environments across residential aged care and retirement living. They are passionate about developing respectful, warm, and genuine relationships where everyone is valued and everyone matters. We are looking for a Personal Care Assistant who will deliver quality care through mutual respect in a warm, caring country environment, empowering residents to make choices about their life, support, and care.

Key Duties (paraphrased & detailed)
Resident-Centred Personal Care & Support
• Deliver high-quality personal care including gentle assistance with bathing, showering, dressing, grooming, toileting, and mobility support (transfers, walking), always following each resident’s individual care plan.
• Promote independence and dignity by encouraging residents to participate in daily activities at their comfort level, supporting them to maintain skills and choice.
• Provide emotional support and genuine companionship, engaging residents in meaningful conversations, reminiscence activities, and recreational pursuits that combat loneliness.

Specialised Care & Health Monitoring
• Assist with specialised care needs including dementia support (using calm, reassuring communication), palliative care (comfort-focused assistance), and behavioural interventions under the guidance of registered nurses.
• Observe and report any changes in residents’ physical or emotional condition (e.g., skin integrity, mood swings, appetite loss) to senior staff in a timely manner.
• Accurately document care provided and contributed to care plan reviews, ensuring resident needs are continuously met and their preferences respected.

Wellness Programs & Therapy Support
• Support therapy and wellness programs by assisting with gentle exercises (range of motion, seated stretching), cognitive stimulation activities (puzzles, memory games), and social outings within the local community.
• Encourage resident participation in group activities that foster connection and engagement, aligned with the “heart of country care” ethos.

Safety, Compliance & Environmental Care
• Adhere strictly to infection control protocols (hand hygiene, PPE use), workplace health & safety policies, and Aged Care Quality Standards to protect vulnerable residents.
• Maintain a clean, hazard-free environment, ensuring resident rooms, communal areas, and bathrooms meet hygiene standards and are free from trip risks.
• Participate in emergency response procedures including fire drills, evacuation support, and basic first aid interventions when required (certification preferred).

Team Collaboration, Communication & Continuous Improvement
• Build trusting relationships with residents’ families, providing empathetic updates on care and addressing concerns with professionalism and warmth.
• Work closely with nurses, allied health professionals (physiotherapists, OTs), and other care staff to ensure a holistic, person-centred approach to resident wellbeing.
• Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives by sharing feedback, participating in staff meetings, attending training sessions, and identifying self-education needs.

Skills & Experience Required
• Certificate III in Aged Care, Individual Support, or equivalent qualification.
• Minimum 1-year full-time experience in a similar role (residential aged care preferred).
• NDIS Worker Screening Clearance (issued within last 5 years) – preferable.
• Up-to-date flu vaccination and full COVID-19 immunisation.
• Satisfactory police check with no disclosures; valid driver’s licence and own reliable transportation.
• Strong teamwork skills, compassionate communication, and a genuine commitment to long-term employment in a regional community setting.

Why Join?
Rewarding work making a real difference in seniors’ lives, ongoing training and professional development, supportive team culture with regular staff recognition, modern country facilities with quality resources, and career growth potential within a respected not-for-profit organisation.

Please note: We are acting as recruitment agents on behalf of our client. Employer details will be provided to shortlisted candidates.

We are offering a highly attractive salary between $82,000 to $92,000 per annum plus superannuation based on the candidate's experience, skills, and other relevant factors.  Located in the heart of Scone, the Scone Willow Tree Hotel is part of a town rich in heritage and famously known as the Horse Capital of Australia. With archival records tracing our presence back to at least 1908, our establishment has stood as a beloved local gathering place for over a century.  Today, we are proud to continue this legacy under an exciting new chapter. While honouring the deep history of our building, we bring a fresh, elevated approach to casual dining—offering honest, flavour-driven food, warm service, and a space where locals, travellers, and workers feel genuinely welcome. Featuring a dynamic menu that spans a dedicated restaurant, bar, café, and specialized gelato bar, we blend classic country warmth with contemporary culinary flair.   Benefits  We are offering a highly attractive salary between $82,000 to $92,000 per annum plus superannuation based on the candidate's experience, skills, and other relevant factors.   Task & responsibilities  As a Chef at Scone Willow Tree Hotel, your tasks include:   Preparing and cooking an elevated, diverse menu that showcases premium cuts (such as Scotch Fillet and Tomahawk steaks), sophisticated mains (like Roasted Duck with pomme purée), contemporary stacks, and refined starters (including Crispy Pork Belly with chimichurri and Steak Tacos).  Handcrafting our signature house pastas (Pasta della Casa), including Meatball Pappardelle, Wagyu Ravioli, and specialized Vodka sauce dishes.  Managing the weekend pizza service, preparing premium artisan pizzas (such as Prosciutto e Burrata and Pulled Pork alla Vodka) during our high-volume Friday and Saturday night trade.  Monitoring the quality of dishes at all stages of preparation and presentation to deliver consistent, high-quality, and beautifully presented meals that meet the expectations of our diverse clientele.  Operating efficiently across a fast-paced service during core trading hours (Tuesday to Saturday, 12:00 PM to 8:30 PM), managing kitchen operation sections to ensure timely prep, execution, and delivery of all orders.  Contributing to menu planning, estimating food and labor costs, and accurately ordering food supplies to support efficient kitchen operations within a tight-knit, collaborative culinary team.  Managing stock levels, rotation, and prep schedules, including freezing and preserving foods correctly to minimize waste and maximize freshness.  Coordinating smoothly with front-of-house staff to maintain seamless service standards, and actively discussing food preparation issues with Managers, Dietitians, and kitchen and waiting staff.  Catering attentively to dietary requirements, confidently managing gluten-free (GFO) and vegetarian (VGO) modifications across the menu.  Demonstrating techniques and advising junior staff on cooking procedures, with the scope to assist in selecting and training new team members.  Explaining, enforcing, and maintaining strict compliance with food safety and hygiene regulations, ensuring immaculate cleanliness and organization across the line, pass, and storage areas.    Qualification & experience  Requirements:   Must possess relevant qualifications  Sound knowledge of food safety, hygiene standards, and safe kitchen practices  Ability to work effectively in a team and communicate clearly during busy service periods  Strong organisational skills with the ability to multi-task in a fast-paced kitchen environment   About Company    Scone Willow Tree Hotel has stood as a local gathering place for over a century, with archival records tracing its presence back to at least 1908, when it was already a recognised establishment within the community. Through the decades, it has remained a familiar meeting point for locals, travelers, and workers, reflecting the strong country hospitality that defines Scone. Fleet Manager
Business: Pacific Automotive Holdings Pty Ltd T/A SIXT Car Rental
Location:  Caringbah NSW 2229
Employment Type: Full-time, Ongoing
Salary: AUD $80,000 – $90,000 per annum plus superannuation
 
Full Job Description
About the Business
Pacific Automotive Holdings Pty Ltd, trading as SIXT Car Rental, is a leading vehicle rental business operating from Caringbah, New South Wales. As part of the internationally recognised SIXT network, the business provides short-term and long-term vehicle rental solutions to private individuals, corporate clients, government organisations, and insurance customers. The branch manages a diverse fleet of passenger vehicles, SUVs, commercial vehicles, and specialty vehicles while delivering high standards of customer service, operational efficiency, and vehicle availability.
Operating within the highly competitive vehicle rental industry, the business coordinates vehicle acquisitions, fleet utilisation, maintenance scheduling, customer bookings, vehicle leasing, logistics, and asset management. Maintaining an efficient and well-managed fleet is critical to ensuring customer satisfaction, maximising vehicle utilisation, controlling operational costs, and supporting the continued growth of the business.
Due to increasing customer demand and ongoing fleet expansion, Pacific Automotive Holdings Pty Ltd is seeking to appoint a dedicated Fleet Manager to oversee the day-to-day management of its vehicle fleet and rental operations.

About the Role
The Fleet Manager is responsible for organising and controlling the buying, leasing, maintenance, utilisation, and operational management of the company's rental vehicle fleet. The role involves coordinating vehicle availability, customer bookings, fleet maintenance, supplier relationships, operational reporting, regulatory compliance, and customer service to ensure efficient business operations.
The successful applicant will possess strong organisational, leadership, communication, and problem-solving skills together with the ability to manage multiple operational priorities within a busy vehicle rental environment.

Key Responsibilities
The successful applicant will be responsible for:
•	Organising and coordinating the purchase, leasing, disposal, maintenance, and utilisation of rental vehicles to ensure optimal fleet performance.
•	Planning and coordinating vehicle servicing, repairs, inspections, registrations, and maintenance schedules to maximise vehicle availability.
•	Liaising with customers to determine vehicle rental requirements, provide advice regarding suitable vehicle types, rental rates, insurance obligations, and resolving customer enquiries and complaints.
•	Receiving vehicle bookings and coordinating vehicle allocation to ensure efficient utilisation of fleet resources.
•	Arranging vehicle collection, delivery, transfers, and logistics between customers, branches, workshops, and service providers.
•	Monitoring fleet availability, utilisation rates, maintenance costs, fuel usage, and operational performance.
•	Maintaining fleet records, operational documentation, maintenance histories, rental agreements, and preparing operational reports for management.
•	Coordinating relationships with external suppliers including repairers, maintenance providers, insurers, registration authorities, and transport contractors.
•	Ensuring compliance with workplace health and safety (WHS) legislation, road transport regulations, vehicle safety requirements, and company operational policies.
•	Developing and implementing procedures that improve fleet efficiency, customer satisfaction, operational performance, and cost control.
•	Supervising operational staff involved in fleet coordination and vehicle preparation while providing ongoing guidance and support.

Requirements
Australian Citizens and Permanent Residents are encouraged to apply.
Applicants should possess:
•	AQF Associate Degree, Advanced Diploma or Diploma in Business, Logistics, Automotive Management, Transport Management, Fleet Management, or a related discipline;
OR
•	At least three years of relevant work experience may substitute for formal qualifications.
Applicants should also demonstrate:
•	Experience managing vehicle fleets, rental operations, transport services, or automotive operations.
•	Strong knowledge of vehicle maintenance scheduling, fleet utilisation, and operational planning.
•	Excellent organisational and communication skills.
•	Strong customer service and stakeholder management capability.
•	Ability to prepare operational reports and maintain accurate fleet records.
•	Experience coordinating vehicle servicing, registrations, repairs, and compliance requirements.
•	Proficiency with Microsoft Office and fleet management software.
•	Knowledge of workplace health and safety legislation and vehicle compliance requirements.
•	Current Australian Driver Licence (preferred).

Work Conditions
•	Full-time, ongoing position.
•	Work location: 60–62 Captain Cook Drive, Caringbah NSW 2229.
•	Competitive salary of AUD $80,000 – $90,000 per annum plus superannuation.
•	Opportunity to work within one of Australia's leading vehicle rental businesses.
•	Professional working environment with ongoing career development opportunities.
Note: Preference will be given to suitably qualified Australian Citizens and Permanent Residents.

result.description:
Chef
Business: Chargrill Charlie's Willoughby
Location: Willoughby NSW 2068
Employment Type: Full-time, Ongoing
Salary: AUD $79,000 – $89,000 per annum plus superannuation

Full Job Description

About the Business
Chargrill Charlie's Willoughby is part of one of Australia's most recognised premium charcoal chicken restaurant brands, renowned for its fresh, high-quality meals and exceptional customer service. The restaurant provides dine-in, takeaway, online ordering, and delivery services to a large and diverse customer base throughout Sydney's Lower North Shore.
Operating within a fast-paced hospitality environment, the restaurant prepares a wide variety of freshly cooked meals including charcoal chicken, burgers, salads, wraps, family meals, and catering orders. Maintaining high food quality, efficient kitchen operations, and exceptional customer service is fundamental to the continued success of the business.
Due to continued customer demand and business growth, Chargrill Charlie's Willoughby is seeking to appoint a dedicated Chef to support the ongoing operation of its commercial kitchen.

About the Role
The Chef is responsible for planning, organising, and coordinating the preparation and cooking of food while ensuring consistently high standards of quality, presentation, food safety, and operational efficiency. The position plays a key role in supporting daily kitchen operations, supervising food preparation activities, maintaining inventory levels, and ensuring efficient service delivery during busy trading periods.
The successful applicant will demonstrate strong culinary skills, excellent organisational ability, leadership capability, and the ability to perform effectively within a high-volume commercial kitchen.


Key Responsibilities
The successful applicant will be responsible for:
•	Planning menus in consultation with management while considering customer demand, seasonal availability, and operational requirements.
•	Estimating food and labour costs and assisting with kitchen budgeting and cost control.
•	Ordering food supplies, monitoring inventory levels, rotating stock, and minimising food wastage.
•	Preparing, cooking, seasoning, and presenting high-quality meals in accordance with company recipes and presentation standards.
•	Monitoring the quality of dishes throughout all stages of preparation, cooking, and presentation.
•	Discussing food preparation requirements and operational issues with management and kitchen staff to ensure efficient workflow.
•	Demonstrating cooking techniques and providing guidance to junior kitchen employees.
•	Supervising food preparation activities to ensure consistency, efficiency, and compliance with company procedures.
•	Ensuring compliance with food safety legislation, HACCP principles, workplace health and safety requirements, and hygiene regulations.
•	Maintaining cleanliness and organisation of kitchen facilities, equipment, and food preparation areas.
•	Assisting in the selection, training, and supervision of kitchen employees.
•	Freezing, storing, preserving, and handling food products in accordance with food safety standards.
•	Supporting efficient kitchen operations during peak service periods while maintaining high food quality and customer satisfaction.

Requirement
Australian Citizens and Permanent Residents are encouraged to apply.
Applicants should possess:
•	AQF Associate Degree, Advanced Diploma or Diploma in Commercial Cookery, Hospitality Management, or a closely related discipline;
OR
•	At least three years of relevant commercial kitchen experience may substitute for formal qualifications.
Applicants should also demonstrate:
•	Experience working as a Chef within a commercial restaurant or hospitality environment.
•	Strong menu planning and food preparation skills.
•	Knowledge of food costing, stock management, and inventory control.
•	Thorough understanding of HACCP, food safety legislation, and workplace health and safety requirements.
•	Excellent leadership, communication, and organisational skills.
•	Ability to supervise kitchen staff and coordinate kitchen workflow.
•	Ability to perform efficiently within a fast-paced, high-volume commercial kitchen.
•	Strong commitment to food quality, presentation, and customer satisfaction.

Work Conditions
•	Full-time, ongoing position.
•	Work location: 201 High Street, Willoughby NSW 2068.
•	Salary: AUD $80,000 – $85,000 per annum plus superannuation.
•	Rotating roster including weekends, evenings, and public holidays.
•	Opportunity to work within one of Australia's leading hospitality brands with ongoing career development opportunities.

Note: Preference will be given to suitably qualified Australian Citizens and Permanent Residents.

result.description:
Head Chef – Surly's Surry Hills

Position Title: Head Chef
Reports To: General Manager
Business: Surly's Hospitality Pty Ltd
Venue: Surly's American Tavern
Location: 182 Campbell Street, Surry Hills NSW 2010
Employment Type: Full-Time, Permanent
Salary: AUD $85,000 per annum plus statutory superannuation

Position Summary

The Head Chef is responsible for the overall leadership and management of the kitchen operations at Surly's American Tavern. This is a full-time senior management position responsible for menu development, food quality, kitchen leadership, financial performance, compliance with food safety legislation, and the efficient operation of a high-volume commercial kitchen.

The role is integral to the ongoing success of the business and requires an experienced chef capable of leading a diverse kitchen team while maintaining consistently high culinary standards, operational efficiency, and profitability.

Key Duties and Responsibilities

- Manage and oversee the daily operations of the kitchen, ensuring efficient service and consistently high food quality.
- Develop, design and implement seasonal menus, daily specials, catering packages and function menus that align with the Surly's brand.
- Plan recipes, portion sizes and menu pricing to maximise profitability while maintaining quality and consistency.
Supervise all food preparation and cooking to ensure presentation, quality, portion control and customer satisfaction standards are consistently achieved.
- Recruit, train, mentor and supervise kitchen employees including Sous Chefs, Chef de Parties, Commis Chefs, Apprentices and Kitchen Hands.
- Prepare staff rosters and allocate duties to ensure efficient kitchen operations and appropriate labour utilisation.
- Monitor labour costs, food costs, gross profit margins and kitchen productivity to achieve business budgets and financial targets.
- Order food, beverages and kitchen supplies, manage supplier relationships and negotiate purchasing where appropriate.
- Monitor inventory levels and implement stock control systems to minimise wastage and maximise profitability.
- Ensure compliance with all Food Safety Standards, HACCP principles, NSW Food Authority requirements and Work Health and Safety legislation.
- Develop, implement and continuously improve kitchen procedures, systems and operational standards.
- Coordinate preventative maintenance of kitchen equipment and arrange repairs as required.
- Work collaboratively with senior management on marketing initiatives, promotional campaigns, special events and business development opportunities.
- Monitor customer feedback and implement continuous improvements to menu offerings and kitchen performance.
- Maintain accurate records relating to stock control, food cost analysis, labour costs, wastage and kitchen performance.
- Ensure high standards of cleanliness, hygiene and food handling practices are maintained throughout the kitchen at all times.
- Foster a positive, professional and high-performing kitchen culture focused on teamwork, accountability and continuous improvement.
- Drive culinary innovation while maintaining the authentic American barbecue style and quality standards that define the Surly's brand.

Skills, Qualifications and Experience

The successful candidate will possess:

- Certificate IV in Commercial Cookery (or equivalent recognised qualification).
- A minimum of five (5) years' relevant experience in a senior chef or Head Chef position.
- Demonstrated experience managing a high-volume commercial kitchen.
- Proven leadership and people management skills with the ability to recruit, train and develop kitchen staff.
- Strong understanding of menu planning, recipe development, food costing and inventory management.
- Excellent knowledge of budgeting, labour management and cost control.
- Comprehensive understanding of Australian food safety legislation, HACCP principles and workplace health and safety requirements.
- Excellent organisational, communication and problem-solving skills.
- Ability to work effectively under pressure while maintaining high standards of food quality and customer service.
- Strong commitment to continuous improvement, innovation and operational excellence.

Key Performance Outcomes

The Head Chef will be expected to:

- Deliver consistently high-quality food and presentation standards.
- Maintain food and labour costs within approved budgets.
- Lead, develop and retain a high-performing kitchen team.
- Ensure full compliance with food safety and workplace health and safety requirements.
- Support the commercial success of the business through effective menu engineering, operational efficiency and cost management.
- Contribute to the ongoing growth and reputation of Surly's American Tavern through culinary leadership and innovation.
